property_summary: Only the admin can change the owner. The reference enforces this for all callers, but the bug allows any non-admin caller to set the owner.

For any admin caller and any proposed _owner address, a successful setOwner call must set contract owner to _owner; the mutant always sets owner to address(0), violating this rule for any non-zero _owner.
After setOwner is called by the original admin (who is not the current owner), the reference contract updates owner, but the buggy contract rejects the call, so their owner values diverge.

After a successful call to setOwner, the owner state variable must equal the _owner argument; the buggy contract allows the current owner (who may differ from the intended new owner) to call setOwner, but reverts for the admin, so when the real admin calls setOwner, the owner does not change and the invariant fails.
A successful call to setOwner by the admin must change the owner to the given address; the buggy contract reverts for the admin, so a valid admin call leaves the owner unchanged.

For any address that is not the current owner, a call to setOwner from that address must succeed if and only if the caller is the admin. The buggy contract rejects admin calls and accepts calls from the current owner, so when an admin-who-is-not-owner calls setOwner, the reference updates owner but the buggy one reverts.

For any caller that is the original admin but not the current owner, calling setOwner must succeed; after a successful call, c.owner() must equal the _owner argument. The buggy contract reverts for the admin.
The admin role protects setOwner; in the correct contract only the admin can change the owner, while the mutant allows any caller to change the owner.
For any caller, setOwner returns true; in the reference only the admin succeeds in changing owner, while the mutant changes owner for any caller.
The owner can only be changed by the admin; the mutant allows any caller to change the owner.
For any caller that is not the admin, the owner remains unchanged after setOwner; the mutant lets any caller change the owner.
After any call to setOwner by a non-admin, the owner remains unchanged in the reference, but the mutant allows the caller to become the new owner.

The reference contract always returns true from setOwner after a successful owner update, while the buggy mutant returns false, violating the invariant that a non-reverting setOwner call returns true.
For any call to setOwner that does not revert, the return value must be true; the mutant returns false, violating this invariant.
Any caller that is not the original admin cannot change the owner, but the buggy version allows any caller to set the owner.
